To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electrical performances of FE memories are strongly correlated to the FE properties of the HfO2 films and that the FE properties of HfO _{2} films are strongly dependent on the film deposition technique.

the physical modeling of FE memory devices and circuits allows for the understanding of the underlying physical mechanisms that determine the device and circuit performance, and for the prediction of the performance of FE memory devices.
the physical models of ferroelectric memory cells are able to capture the main electrical characteristics of the devices and to provide a physical interpretation of the experimental results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials, device concepts, and architectures for next-generation nonvolatile memories, neuromorphic computing, and in-memory computing.
the physical understanding of FE memory cells, the development of compact models for FE devices, and the application of FE devices in emerging computing applications.
the physical and circuit modeling of FE memories and devices, which is a prerequisite for the design of next generation FE memories and devices for neuromorphic computing and in memory computing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FE memory devices based on HfO2 are very promising and have a high potential to become a key technology in the next generation of high-density memory devices and neuromorphic computing applications.
the FE memory device performances can be improved by optimizing both the FE material properties and device design.
the FE HfOX-based memory devices are promising for high-density storage applications, and for neuromorphic applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we can now provide the first complete picture on the physical origin of memory window and retention time in ferroelectric memory devices, which is the first step towards the engineering of high-performance ferroelectric memory cells and circuits.
the FE memory device performance is mainly limited by the FE switching speed and the FE switching energy.
a combination of physical modeling and circuit simulations provides a powerful tool to understand and optimize the performances of the FE memory devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FE memory performance is mainly governed by the FE properties of the HfO2 layer, which can be tailored through engineering the HfO _{2} stoichiometry, thickness and the presence of defects.
FE memory cells can be used to realize a wide range of functionalities and performances by simply changing the FE layer thickness.
the FE Hf-O2 based memories and devices are very sensitive to the interface quality and the presence of oxygen vacancies.
